rationale: The unsized [u8]-transmuted view becomes a lifetime-parameterised struct holding &'a [u8], so construction is a plain struct literal and the transmute disappears with the representation change.
The raw-pointer deref of the map's entry count is replaced by an ordinary read of the iterator's own len field, so the unsafe block is simply dropped and nothing else is needed.

The out-of-bounds one-past-end pointer built with get_unchecked is replaced by plain usize address arithmetic over data.as_ptr(); this is integer overflow bookkeeping, which fits no checked-API, slice, init or wrapper class.

rationale: ptr::swap over &mut self[a]/&mut self[b] is replaced by a temporary-based swap of Copy column vectors; the aliasing unsafe was never needed.
ptr::swap is replaced by a temporary-based swap of Copy elements, which the Copy supertrait bound proves safe without any raw-pointer aliasing.
set_len that exposed uninitialised bytes to read_exact is replaced by resize(.., 0), zero-initialising the buffer before it is read into.
get_unchecked table access becomes a bounds-checked index, and the added 286|287 arm rejects reserved length codes with an InvalidData error instead of reading out of range.
The mem::uninitialized placeholder plus mem::replace/mem::forget dance is replaced by take_mut::take, a safe crate helper that moves the whole struct out and hands it back.
msys_tty_on became a safe function, so only the unsafe block wrapping it had to be removed.

The uninitialised-memory seed is replaced by a deterministic seed summed from the prefix bytes; a real replacement, but it redesigns where the seed comes from and fits no memory/checked/slice mechanism.

rationale: Drop now delegates the raw-pointer cleanup to the safe take method instead of loading the pointer and reconstructing P itself, and into_raw loses its unsafe qualifier.
The zero-length Vec-with-capacity representation becomes a Vec<Option<T>> whose length is the slot count, so no set_len or uninitialised slots are needed.

The reserved-but-uninitialised buffer reached via get_unchecked_mut is replaced by resize(len, 0) plus as_mut_slice/as_slice, so the read target is initialised and the returned slice is length-checked.
with_capacity plus set_len uninitialised storage is replaced by vec![0; count], so read_exact fills initialised memory.
The unsafe with_capacity_non_copy constructor is replaced by a call to the safe from_vec constructor, which encapsulates the raw-parts construction behind the CopyElem bound.
The ManuallyDrop plus Vec::from_raw_parts reinterpretation is replaced by VecVoid::from_vec, a safe constructor that takes ownership of the Vec and records its parts internally.
The byte-level from_raw_parts copy becomes a bounds-checked copy_from_slice that reports a length mismatch with None instead of invoking UB.
Construction is delegated to the safe from_vec constructor instead of the unsafe with_type_non_copy.
The manual aligned dummy pointer built with NonNull::new_unchecked is replaced by the safe std constructor NonNull::dangling().
set_len that exposed uninitialised bytes to read_exact is replaced by resize(.., 0), zero-initialising the buffer before the read.

The with_capacity plus set_len output vector becomes an explicitly initialised vec!, and the reusable scanline buffer becomes vec![Default::default(); width]; the chunks_mut slicing is secondary to that initialisation change.

The AtomicPtr plus unsafe Box::from_raw/ptr-deref registry is replaced by a Mutex<RegistryState> owning Option<Box<dyn Any + Send>>, retrieved through a checked Any downcast.
The unchecked drop plus the raw occupancy-bit clearing loop are replaced by the safe remove_at helper, which clears the bit before taking the value out.
as_type_ptr is now a safe method, so the unsafe block around it was simply removed.
The raw-pointer cast back to PyAny is replaced by a direct borrow of the embedded field; PyAny already owns the UnsafeCell in both versions, so the cast and deref were redundant.
